paragraphs: This paper studies how people learn collectively when each person chooses only what currently seems rewarding. Online reviews motivate the setting: earlier choices provide information that later users can draw on, but individual users do not deliberately try uncertain options to help the group learn. The collective process follows a multi-armed bandit protocol.

The analysis covers a broad family of short-sighted decision rules rather than a single algorithm. These rules must be consistent with parameterized confidence intervals around the options’ expected rewards. Within that framework, the authors derive pronounced failures of exploration and matching positive results. Together, these results characterize both difficulties and possibilities for learning under the behaviors studied.

A notable special case concerns the greedy algorithm, which acts on currently available reward estimates without explicitly encouraging exploration. The paper provides general theoretical results about its failures. This gives a mathematical basis for designing bandit algorithms that actively gather information: individually appealing choices can leave the collective learning process poorly informed.
neurips-2023-bandit-social-learning-unde.tldr: The paper characterizes when short-sighted bandit decisions fail to explore, providing theoretical support for deliberate exploration.

paragraphs: Updating a small part of an optimization problem at a time can make computation efficient. Applying this idea to sequential games is difficult because the components of a player's strategy are linked. Their feasible strategy spaces do not have the separable structure that ordinary coordinate methods typically exploit.

The paper develops a cyclic, coordinate-descent-like method for sequence-form strategies in extensive-form games. It uses the recursive structure of updates associated with dilated regularizers to construct partial updates despite those dependencies. For two-player zero-sum games, the method has an O(1/T) convergence rate to a Nash equilibrium and avoids the worst-case polynomial dependence on block count common to cyclic methods.

Experiments show that the method usually improves on first-order alternatives such as mirror prox and sometimes outperforms CFR+. The authors also introduce a restarting heuristic. Empirically, restarting can accelerate both their method and existing solvers, with very large improvements in some cases. These speedups are experimental findings, while the convergence rate is a theoretical guarantee.
neurips-2023-block-coordinate-methods-an.tldr: A cyclic partial-update method offers provable convergence for sequential zero-sum games, while restarting empirically accelerates several game solvers.

paragraphs: EEG recordings can vary across people, recording sessions, and hardware, creating difficulties when a prediction model encounters new data. This paper addresses that variability through signal normalization. Its method, Convolutional Monge Mapping Normalization, or CMMN, changes the incoming signals rather than requiring the prediction model to be retrained.

CMMN filters signals so their power spectral density, which describes how signal power is distributed across frequencies, approaches a shared reference. That reference is a Wasserstein barycenter estimated from the training data. The method relies on new closed-form solutions for optimal transport mappings and barycenters, allowing individual adaptation when new data arrive at test time.

Experiments on sleep EEG show significant, consistent performance improvements across the neural architectures tested. These improvements cover transfers between subjects, sessions, and datasets recorded with different hardware. The reported gains are comparable to those from much more computationally intensive domain adaptation methods. CMMN can also be combined with those methods for further improvement, making the normalization approach complementary to model-level adaptation.
neurips-2023-convolution-monge-mapping-n.tldr: CMMN aligns EEG frequency profiles to a training-derived reference, improving sleep-data prediction across recording conditions without retraining the predictor.

paragraphs: DreamHuman generates realistic three-dimensional human avatars from written descriptions. Its goal includes making those avatars usable in different poses. This addresses several problems identified in earlier text-to-3D approaches: limited control and resolution, fixed generated poses, and difficulty maintaining plausible human proportions in complex human figures.

The method combines large text-to-image synthesis models, neural radiance fields, and statistical human body models within one optimization framework. These components bring together text-guided appearance generation and a representation of human shape. The resulting avatars include detailed textures and geometric deformations learned separately for each instance, covering both rigid changes and changes that alter shape.

The authors demonstrate avatars with varied clothing, appearance, skin tones, and body shapes that can be animated or posed differently. They report higher visual fidelity than both general text-to-3D methods and earlier text-based avatar generators. The contribution therefore joins visual quality with pose flexibility: the generated human is a dynamic 3D model rather than merely an appealing result in one fixed configuration.
neurips-2023-dreamhuman-animatable-3d-av.tldr: DreamHuman combines text-to-image models, neural radiance fields, and body models to generate realistic, animatable human avatars from text.

paragraphs: Anomaly detection becomes difficult when ordinary behavior changes over time. Methods designed for stable multivariate time series can mistake this drift for abnormal events and produce false alarms. D³R addresses unstable data by combining a dynamic decomposition stage with a reconstruction stage in an end-to-end trainable network.

For decomposition, the method uses data-time mix-attention to work with long-period multivariate sequences. This is intended to overcome the restricted view of a local sliding window. For reconstruction, it addresses the information bottleneck, a consequential design choice that is difficult to set. Noise diffusion controls this bottleneck externally, and the network reconstructs the noise-corrupted data directly.

External control means the bottleneck can change without requiring the model to be retrained for that change. Across the real-world datasets studied, the authors report significant gains over existing methods, including an average relative improvement of 11% over previous leading models. The findings support combining longer-range decomposition with adjustable reconstruction when detecting anomalies in data whose behavior is changing.
neurips-2023-drift-doesn-t-matter-dynami.tldr: D³R combines dynamic decomposition and diffusion-controlled reconstruction to improve anomaly detection in drifting multivariate time series.

paragraphs: This paper uses human personality assessment as a structured way to study language-model behavior. The central questions are whether psychometric tests can provide principled, quantitative measurements of machine behavior and whether prompts can induce particular personality patterns. The focus is on observable responses assessed through a standardized framework.

The authors introduce the Machine Personality Inventory, or MPI, drawing on established personality inventories and the Big Five framework. They systematically evaluate language models with this tool and report initial evidence that it is useful for studying their behavior. The contribution is a common assessment approach through which differences in model responses can be examined quantitatively.

The paper also introduces Personality Prompting, abbreviated P², to induce specific personalities in a controllable manner. The authors report diverse behaviors that can be checked through assessment. Taken together, the measurement tool and prompting method connect behavioral evaluation with behavioral steering. The proposed use of personality as an indicator for downstream tasks remains a direction for future research, rather than a demonstrated result across those tasks.
neurips-2023-evaluating-and-inducing-per.tldr: The paper introduces a personality-based inventory for evaluating language-model behavior and a prompting method for controllably inducing personality patterns.

paragraphs: Black-box optimization searches for good inputs when an objective is accessed through evaluations. As the number of input dimensions grows, choosing useful evaluations efficiently becomes challenging. This paper introduces Rank-1 Lattice Targeted Sampling, or RLTS, to improve the sampling stage of stochastic optimization methods.

RLTS uses randomized rank-1 lattice Quasi-Monte Carlo sampling. The structure enables local exact Gaussian-process training and inference in O(n log n) time for a batch of n samples. The authors also develop a coordinate search procedure with the same time complexity and a closed-form way to construct the lattices. These components make targeted sampling computationally practical within the broader optimization process.

The paper reports that incorporating RLTS improves query efficiency while reaching higher-dimensional problems than Bayesian optimization. Experiments cover challenging benchmark functions and black-box prompt fine-tuning for large language models. The findings concern both the cost of deciding where to sample and the usefulness of the resulting evaluations: faster sampling computations support a more query-efficient search in the tested settings.
neurips-2023-fast-rank-1-lattice-targete.tldr: RLTS uses structured lattice samples to make targeted black-box search computationally fast and empirically more query-efficient.

paragraphs: Recurrent neural networks can struggle to learn from distant events because gradients grow excessively or shrink away across many time steps. Gradient flossing addresses this through the network's forward dynamics. It pushes Lyapunov exponents, which describe how tiny perturbations grow or contract, toward zero during learning.

The method regularizes these exponents using backpropagation through differentiable linear algebra. Its influence extends beyond controlling overall gradient size: it also controls the condition number of the long-term Jacobian. That matters because useful error signals need to propagate across multiple directions, not merely retain a reasonable total magnitude.

The authors find that applying flossing before task training improves success rates and convergence speed on long-horizon tasks. For challenging tasks, applying it during training can further extend the time span that backpropagation through time can bridge. Experiments cover different recurrent architectures and temporal complexities, and the paper provides a simple implementation. The results support regulating dynamical stability as a practical way to mitigate exploding and vanishing gradients.
neurips-2023-gradient-flossing-improving.tldr: Gradient flossing regularizes recurrent-network dynamics to stabilize gradients and improve learning over long time horizons.

paragraphs: Datathons bring people together to collaborate, learn, and develop ideas quickly using data. Their potential depends partly on how well organizers handle the data involved. This paper addresses a practical obstacle: organizations often lack clear guidance and established practices for the data-related issues that can arise while arranging these events.

The authors develop an organizer-facing guide from their own experience running more than 80 datathon challenges with more than 60 partner organizations. That experience supplies the basis for a framework intended to help organizers navigate data-related complexity. The contribution is practical guidance grounded in organizing work, with the focus placed on supporting the conditions under which participants can work effectively.

The paper applies the proposed framework to 10 case studies. These applications show how the guidance can be brought to concrete datathon settings. Its value lies in turning accumulated organizing experience into a resource that others can use when handling data challenges, complementing the collaborative and rapid-development aims that make datathons attractive.
neurips-2023-how-to-data-in-datathons-bf.tldr: The paper turns extensive datathon-organizing experience into a data-management guide and applies its framework to 10 case studies.

paragraphs: Some image-protection methods add changes that people cannot readily see but that interfere with diffusion-based generation. The aim is to discourage unauthorized uses such as imitating an artist's style or maliciously editing an image. IMPRESS evaluates how resilient these protections are when someone attempts to purify the protected image.

The method starts from an observation about reconstruction: visually imperceptible perturbations can produce perceptible disagreement between an image and its diffusion-reconstructed version. IMPRESS uses this inconsistency to formulate an optimization strategy for purification. The resulting processing may weaken the perturbations' protective effect and allow forms of usage that the original protection was designed to obstruct.

The authors use the platform to evaluate several contemporary protection methods and propose it as a testing resource for future methods. The contribution is therefore an evaluation approach tied to a specific potential weakness in protective perturbations. It provides a way to examine whether protection remains effective after purification, without establishing that every perturbation-based defense will necessarily fail.
neurips-2023-impress-evaluating-the-resi.tldr: IMPRESS tests image-protection perturbations using reconstruction-based purification that may weaken their resistance to unauthorized diffusion-model usage.

paragraphs: This paper develops a way to improve adversarial robustness by transferring knowledge from a robust pretrained model. Its approach, Information Bottleneck Distillation, connects teacher-to-student learning with the information bottleneck principle. The aim is to shape internal features so they retain information useful for prediction while reducing their dependence on the input.

The method has two complementary distillation strategies. Robust soft-label distillation increases mutual information between latent features and output predictions. Adaptive feature distillation transfers relevant knowledge from the teacher to the student and reduces mutual information between inputs and latent features. These strategies correspond to the two optimization directions of the information bottleneck.

The authors evaluate the resulting robustness against adversarial attackers including PGD and AutoAttack. Their experiments report significant improvements, supporting the effectiveness of this combination of robust prior knowledge and information-bottleneck objectives. The work's main contribution is the coordinated design of the two transfers: one strengthens prediction-relevant information, while the other shapes how much input information the internal representation preserves.
neurips-2023-improving-adversarial-robus.tldr: Information Bottleneck Distillation transfers robust teacher knowledge through two complementary objectives that empirically improve adversarial robustness.

paragraphs: Federated learning distributes training across clients, creating opportunities for backdoor attacks. Defenses can impose substantial computation, which is a problem in resource-constrained settings. The authors investigate pruning as a practical defense but find that traditional pruning suffers from a poison-coupling effect in federated learning that substantially weakens its effectiveness.

Lockdown changes the training protocol to isolate the subspaces used by different clients. It introduces randomness when initializing those subspaces and combines subspace pruning with recovery to separate malicious and benign contributions. A quorum-consensus mechanism then removes malicious or dummy parameters from the global model. These procedures are designed together to reduce the poison-coupling problem.

Experiments show stronger and more consistent backdoor defense than the representative existing approaches considered. The paper also reports communication efficiency and reduced model complexity, properties relevant when clients have limited resources. The contribution therefore includes both a defense mechanism and changes to the training structure that support a less demanding federated learning process in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2023-lockdown-backdoor-defense-f.tldr: Lockdown isolates client training subspaces and uses pruning, recovery, and consensus to improve federated backdoor defense while reducing resource demands.

paragraphs: Meta-black-box optimization with reinforcement learning uses a learned higher-level process to reduce manual tuning of underlying optimizers. Comparing approaches is difficult without a common evaluation setting. MetaBox addresses that gap with a benchmark platform specifically designed for developing and assessing methods in this area.

The platform provides a flexible algorithmic template for implementing different designs. Its evaluation collection contains more than 300 problem instances spanning synthetic and realistic scenarios. It also includes 19 baseline methods covering traditional black-box optimization and more recent reinforcement-learning-based meta-optimization approaches. Three standardized performance metrics provide a shared basis for assessing methods from multiple perspectives.

The authors demonstrate the platform through a broad benchmarking study of existing methods. The stated contribution is the infrastructure for rigorous comparison and deeper analysis, rather than a claim that one new optimizer dominates the others. By bringing implementations, problem instances, comparison methods, and measurements into one open-source platform, MetaBox supports a more consistent development and evaluation process for the field.
neurips-2023-metabox-a-benchmark-platfor.tldr: MetaBox provides shared problems, baselines, metrics, and implementation support for evaluating reinforcement-learning-based meta-black-box optimization.

paragraphs: This paper studies repeated price competition between two firms that lack information about each other. Consumer demand follows a multinomial logit model and depends on both current prices and reference prices. Because reference prices update over time, today's competition is connected to future periods rather than being an isolated pricing decision.

The authors use a stationary Nash equilibrium to describe a stable long-run outcome. They propose online projected gradient ascent, in which firms adjust prices using derivatives of log-revenue available through market feedback. The algorithm therefore operates with the feedback specified by the model without requiring knowledge of the competitor.

The analysis establishes convergence of both prices and reference prices to the unique stationary equilibrium under diminishing step sizes. This holds despite the absence of familiar convergence properties such as strong monotonicity and variational stability. With appropriate step sizes, the authors prove an O(1/t) rate. Within the modeled setting, these results connect decentralized price adjustment with no-regret learning and a stable market outcome.
neurips-2023-no-regret-learning-in-dynam.tldr: Under the paper's demand model and step-size conditions, feedback-based price updates converge to a unique stable equilibrium despite reference-price dynamics.

paragraphs: Evaluating fairness in generated images often depends on classifiers that identify sensitive attributes. This paper finds that the existing measurement framework can produce substantial errors even when those classifiers are highly accurate. As a result, apparent improvements in a generator's fairness may partly reflect errors in the measurement process.

The authors introduce CLassifier Error-Aware Measurement, or CLEAM, to account statistically for inaccuracies in sensitive-attribute classification. The framework substantially reduces measurement error while adding little overhead. In the reported StyleGAN2 gender example, the measurement error falls from 4.98% to 0.62%. This improvement concerns the reliability of evaluation rather than a change to the generator itself.

The paper also uses CLEAM to assess text-to-image generators and generative adversarial networks, finding considerable biases in the models examined. Together, the results show why measuring fairness requires attention to the evaluator's own errors. They cast doubt on previously reported improvements without establishing that all such improvements are invalid, and provide a more error-aware approach to assessing future claims.
neurips-2023-on-measuring-fairness-in-ge.tldr: CLEAM accounts for sensitive-attribute classifier errors to make generative-model fairness measurements substantially more accurate.

paragraphs: Learning from events far back in a sequence requires assigning credit across long time spans. Online learning offers a potentially efficient way to do this in recurrent neural networks, but existing approaches have faced a tradeoff: they either scale poorly or struggle to learn long-range dependencies compared with offline backpropagation.

The proposed algorithm uses independent recurrent modules within a multilayer network. This architectural structure enables an online learning procedure whose memory and computational requirements are only twice those of a single inference pass. The efficiency claim is therefore tied to how recurrence is organized, with modularity supporting the learning calculation.

Experiments on synthetic memory problems and the Long Range Arena benchmark show competitive performance. These findings support the possibility of learning long-range dependencies with a relatively inexpensive online algorithm, addressing both efficiency and capability in the tested settings. The authors also identify implications for understanding learning in the brain and for neuromorphic computing, presenting those as promising perspectives opened by the result.
neurips-2023-online-learning-of-long-ran.tldr: Independent recurrent modules enable competitive online learning of long-range dependencies at twice the memory and computation of a single inference pass.

paragraphs: Many graph neural networks implicitly expect connected nodes to share labels. That expectation can be unhelpful in heterophilous graphs, where connections more often join nodes from different classes. This paper proposes Low-Rank Graph Neural Network, or LRGNN, as a framework applicable to both similar-label and different-label connection patterns.

The approach builds on an analysis showing that a signed graph's global label relationship matrix has low rank. The authors use this structure to predict label relationships by solving a robust low-rank matrix approximation problem. Prior results establishing perfect recovery under certain conditions motivate this choice; the recovery statement is conditional rather than a universal guarantee for every graph.

In experiments, the estimated matrix closely resembles the actual label relationship matrix. The authors highlight its block-diagonal structure and the differing distributions of within-class and between-class entries as useful properties for graph modeling. The contribution is a global way to represent label relationships, giving the network information beyond the assumption that a local edge should imply a shared class.
neurips-2023-predicting-global-label-rel.tldr: LRGNN predicts global label relationships through robust low-rank approximation to support graph learning under both homophily and heterophily.

paragraphs: This paper investigates why an additional neural-network layer can help a model learn useful features. Much existing theory focuses on two-layer networks, leaving hierarchical feature learning less understood. The authors analyze three-layer networks trained by layer-wise gradient descent and establish richer feature-learning capabilities in the settings studied.

Their general theorem bounds the number of samples and network width sufficient for low test error when the target has a specified hierarchical structure. They apply the framework to single-index models and functions of quadratic features. For the quadratic-feature setting, their sample-complexity guarantee improves on existing guarantees for two-layer networks, with the improvement depending on efficient learning of nonlinear features.

The authors also construct a function that gradient descent can learn efficiently with a three-layer network but that a two-layer network cannot learn efficiently. This gives a concrete optimization-based separation between the depths. The result supplies a provable benefit of depth under the analyzed structure and training procedure, rather than a general claim that three layers always outperform two.
neurips-2023-provable-guarantees-for-non.tldr: The paper proves that three-layer networks can efficiently learn nonlinear features that yield advantages over two-layer networks in specified settings.

paragraphs: Matrix completion aims to recover a matrix from observed entries. Nonconvex formulations offer computational appeal, but previous convergence proofs for gradient descent have required careful initialization or explicit regularization. This paper studies the symmetric rank-one case and proves recovery of the ground truth from a sufficiently small random initialization.

The analysis follows the optimization trajectory before it reaches the region where local convergence applies. It shows that this region is entered within a logarithmic number of iterations. The authors also provide an upper bound on initialization size sufficient for convergence, and show that more observed samples allow a larger initialization.

A central mechanism is gradient descent's implicit regularization: throughout the trajectory, it prevents individual entries from becoming much larger than the others. This controlled behavior helps explain why the simple procedure can succeed without the additional safeguards used in earlier analyses. The result is specific to symmetric rank-one matrix completion, and the initialization bound is a sufficient condition rather than a claim that every larger initialization fails.
neurips-2023-rank-1-matrix-completion-wi.tldr: For symmetric rank-one matrix completion, gradient descent provably recovers the ground truth from sufficiently small random initialization.

paragraphs: Visual tracking uses a template or earlier video frames to help locate an object in the current frame. However, the historical information useful for one search region or moment may be unhelpful for another. Using every available reference feature can introduce redundancy and information that harms tracking.

This paper proposes a tracker built around relevance attention and a global representation memory. The attention mechanism accesses information across frames to dynamically construct a memory suited to the current frame. It then lets the search region read relevant historical information from that memory. Both memory construction and retrieval therefore adapt to the current tracking problem.

The authors evaluate the method on five challenging datasets and report competitive tracking performance at 71 frames per second. These results support selective use of history as an effective tracking strategy. The contribution goes beyond retaining reference features: it makes decisions about which past information to organize and retrieve, with the aim of reducing redundant features and limiting the influence of harmful ones.
neurips-2023-reading-relevant-feature-fr.tldr: A relevance-guided memory helps a visual tracker select useful historical features, achieving competitive results at 71 frames per second.

paragraphs: Many unsupervised anomaly detectors use features from a frozen encoder pretrained on natural images. Those features may fit industrial inspection or medical imaging poorly. ReContrast addresses this mismatch by adapting the whole network to the target domain, reducing its dependence on representations shaped by the original pretraining domain.

The method begins with feature reconstruction, where reconstruction errors provide evidence of anomalies. It incorporates elements of contrastive learning so that the encoder and decoder can be optimized together. These elements are designed to prevent unstable training, collapsed patterns, and an identical shortcut, problems that would undermine the usefulness of reconstruction errors.

The authors test ReContrast on two industrial defect-detection benchmarks and three medical-image anomaly-detection tasks, reporting improvements over current leading methods. The findings support joint adaptation of feature extraction and reconstruction across the examined domains. The key contribution is enabling that adaptation while preserving a useful anomaly signal, rather than treating the pretrained encoder's representation as fixed throughout target-domain learning.
neurips-2023-recontrast-domain-specific-.tldr: ReContrast combines contrastive learning with feature reconstruction to adapt entire anomaly-detection networks to industrial and medical image domains.

paragraphs: Large vision-language models learn from vast collections of image-caption pairs, but malicious pairs can introduce targeted poisoning or backdoors. RoCLIP modifies contrastive pretraining to disrupt the associations that these attacks depend on. Its defense acts during model training, when image and text relationships are being learned.

Every few epochs, RoCLIP matches each image to its most similar caption within a large, changing pool of random captions instead of using its original caption. Image and text augmentations further support the defense and model performance. This periodically replaces potentially poisoned pairings with matches chosen through the model's similarity mechanism.

In the reported experiments, targeted poisoning success drops from 93.75% to 12.5%, while backdoor success falls to 0%. Linear-probe performance improves by 10%, with similar zero-shot performance to CLIP. More frequent matching also handles strong attacks containing up to 1% poisoned examples, maintaining a 12.5% attack success rate. That stronger defense trades off performance on some tasks, making matching frequency a consequential choice.
neurips-2023-robust-contrastive-language.tldr: RoCLIP periodically rematches images with captions to disrupt poisoning and backdoor associations, substantially reducing attack success in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Lipschitz bandits involve choosing actions from a continuous space where nearby actions have related expected rewards. This paper adds adversarial corruption to that setting: an adaptive attacker can alter the observed stochastic rewards, subject to a total budget C accumulated across the time horizon T.

The analysis distinguishes attackers by what they know when corrupting feedback. A weak attacker does not know the current action before the attack, while a strong attacker can observe it. The authors develop robust algorithms for both cases, including when the learner is not told the corruption budget. They establish sublinear-regret results under their analyzed corruption setting.

The paper also provides a lower bound for each adversary type and shows that its algorithm is optimal in the strong-adversary case. Experiments illustrate effectiveness against two classic attack types. Together, the theoretical and empirical results clarify how robust learning depends on an attacker's access to the current decision, while extending continuous-action bandit methods to feedback that may have been deliberately distorted.
neurips-2023-robust-lipschitz-bandits-to.tldr: The paper develops corruption-robust Lipschitz bandit algorithms and proves optimality for the analyzed strong-adversary setting.

paragraphs: Adversarial robustness for tabular data presents challenges that differ from those emphasized in image and text research. Categorical features do not directly fit existing optimization procedures. Meanwhile, effective tabular classifiers such as boosted trees and random forests cannot directly use robustness methods designed specifically for neural networks.

The paper addresses both issues with universal robust embeddings tailored to categorical data. It first supports adversarially robust deep-network training, then transfers robustness through the learned embeddings to other classifiers. The embeddings are produced using a bilevel alternating minimization framework, connecting representation learning with the robustness objective.

The authors show that boosted trees and random forests can use these embeddings to gain robustness without undergoing adversarial training themselves, while preserving high tabular-data accuracy. They also report better results than existing techniques within a practical threat model suited to tabular data. The contribution is a transferable representation: robustness learned through a neural approach can benefit other classifier families under the evaluated threat model.
neurips-2023-transferable-adversarial-ro.tldr: Robust categorical embeddings transfer adversarial robustness from deep-network training to boosted trees and random forests while preserving high accuracy.

paragraphs: VoxDet detects previously unseen object instances using multiple template views. Two-dimensional matching can struggle when an object rotates or becomes partly hidden. The method introduces a geometry-aware representation that brings three-dimensional information into the task of detecting an instance in a two-dimensional image.

Its template voxel aggregation module maps template images into 3D voxel features and combines them using their camera poses. A reconstruction objective helps pretrain this mapping. The query voxel matching module then maps query images into the same representation, estimates relative rotation, and compares aligned voxels. This uses encoded geometry to improve both matching accuracy and efficiency.

The authors also introduce RoboTools, containing 20 recorded object instances, 24 cluttered scenarios, and more than 9,000 box annotations. Experiments on RoboTools, LineMod-Occlusion, and YCB-video show substantial improvements over several 2D baselines alongside faster operation. The findings support representing and aligning object geometry explicitly within the matching process to improve resilience to pose changes and occlusion in the evaluated detection tasks.
neurips-2023-voxdet-voxel-learning-for-n.tldr: VoxDet converts template and query images into aligned voxel features to improve novel-instance detection under pose changes and occlusion.
